title.big: Read a dynamometer card, find the fault
title.desc: Ask in plain English. Deckhand asks for what it needs, runs the calculation, and sends back a report you can keep.

turns.html: One of my rod-pumped wells is acting up and the dynamometer card looks off. Can you read the card and tell me what's wrong with the pump?

Happy to read it. A few things so I diagnose the right card:
  • The card itself — surface card or pump (downhole) card? Load-vs-position trace is what I work from.
  • Rod string & pump — rod diameter and length, pump bore and setting depth?
  • Stroke & speed — surface stroke length and strokes-per-minute, plus the gearbox rating?
I classify the common rod-pump conditions — fluid pound, gas interference, pump tagging, valve leaks, tubing movement. If it looks like none of those, I'll say so rather than force a label.
Pump card attached. 1.0" rods, 5,000 ft string. 1.75" pump set at 5,000 ft. 144" stroke at 10 SPM, 640,000 in-lb gearbox.

Got it — pump card, 1.0" rods to a 1.75" pump at 5,000 ft, 144" × 10 SPM. I'll trace the load-vs-position loop, pull the card-shape features, and run the classifier to name the condition and rank the alternatives. Running it now…

Here's what the card is telling us:
FindingValueRead from
ConditionPump tagging100% confidence
Pump fillage75.9%downhole card area
Production338 bbl/dayeffective stroke
Rod string⚠ Buckling detectedload-spike at bottom
The plunger is making mechanical contact with the standing valve (or the top of the pump) at the bottom of the stroke — that's the load spike. It also shows mechanical buckling in the rod string. Differential: tagging 100%, traveling-valve leak 0%, tubing movement 0%. I'd shorten the stroke or raise the pump before the rods take more damage.

report.title: Dynacard Diagnostics
report.inputs:
Well
SIM-PUMP-TAGGING-711

Rod string
Diameter 1.0" · Length 5,000 ft

Pump
Bore 1.75" · Setting depth 5,000 ft

Surface unit
Stroke length 144" · 10 SPM · Gearbox 640,000 in-lb

Card
Pump (downhole) card · load vs. position
report.methodology:
1 · Trace the load-vs-position loop from the pump card.
2 · Extract card-shape features (the Bezerra projections) that describe the loop.
3 · Run the trained classifier (GradientBoosting v1.0, 5,400 synthetic cards, 89.4% cross-validated) to name the condition.
4 · Rank the alternatives as a differential diagnosis, not a single guess.
5 · Compute pump fillage from the downhole card area and convert effective stroke to a production rate.
6 · Flag rod-string buckling from the bottom-of-stroke load spike.
